So, the kind of pirates you're thinking of operated for a very small period of time, and much of the popular image of the pirates came from works of fiction published years after. In someways it's similar to the idea of the American "Old West" period, where the fictions written and performed a generation after defined the period more than the actual events.

The "golden age" of piracy is about thirty years or so, at the start of the 18th century. Typically French or English sailors operating around the Caribbean.

I would recommend avoiding Blackbeard. Charles Vane is, perhaps, the best representation of what we think of when we think of pirates. He had a pretty active career that spanned six years before he was hanged. That's not a bad run, under the circumstances. You weren't going to retire rich in this game. The drug cartels are not a bad model to think of when it comes to pirates. Limited success, once and a while flashy wealth, and normally an end to your life as a result of violence.
